newsitem.title: UK: Nomura says unlikely to control Annington.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says unlikely to control Annington.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd is unlikely ever to take control of Annington Homes, the company it set up to buy the British services' married quarters estate for 1.66 billion stg, a Nomura executive said on Wednesday.

Guy Hands, managing director of the Japanese firm's Nomura International unit, told the defence committee of Britain's Parliament that Nomura held just over 75 percent of the warrants issued by the company which are convertible into shares.
Hands agreed that if Nomura decided to exercise conversion rights, which it could only do after senior bank debt is paid off in five to 10 years time, it would control Annington.
But he added: "My expectation is that at that point in time the company would probably be floated."

"My guess is that it is very unlikely Nomura will ever convert those warrants to equity," he added. "Nomura is not in the business of owning property companies. It is in the business of providing finance -- as part of this finance it received warrants."
Annington completed the purchase of 57,400 servicemen's homes from the Ministry of Defence last week.
The privatisation had been politically controversial even before it emerged that a foreign bank was so heavily involved in the successful bidding consortium.

The majority of Annington's modest current issued equity is owned by British property company AMEC Plc. Other warrant holders are New York-based Blackrock Capital Finance LP with 23 percent and Electra Fleming with 1-1/2 percent.

Abbey National Treasury Services, Hambros Bank, Midland Bank and Royal Bank of Scotland also formed part of the bidding consortium, which launched three bonds totalling 903 million stg last week. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
